mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such regimes are not statistically lower than during stable rate periods (p > 0.05 in t-test)

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to market anticipation of rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: Inflation exceeds 3% for >6 months without a subsequent negative 20-day forward return (cumulative frequency < 30%)

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of more than 0.5% monthly for two months is accompanied by a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >0.5% in one month and >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such labor expansions

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% followed by a rebound of 1% the next month indicates cyclical weakness, which is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate economic softening.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops >2% in one month and recovers >1% in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such patterns are not significantly lower than during steady-state growth (p > 0.1 in t-test)

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (housing starts) exceeding 5% for two months signal robust construction activity, which amplifies optimism and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% in one month and >2% in the next
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such periods are not higher than average (median < 0.5%)

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as labor market tightness supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and remains below for 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during such episodes

mechanism_narrative: A sustained dual decline in both FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 (GDP momentum) for two consecutive months suggests a coinciding softening in monetary policy and economic output, which predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases for 2 months AND GDPC1 decreases for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such dual declines are not statistically negative (p > 0.05)

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 4% in a single month followed by two consecutive months of flat retail sales, the S&P 5-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to supply-side weakness in consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >4% in one month and remains flat for the next two months
regime_hint: early signs of consumer demand contraction
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns during such episodes are not negative (p > 0.05)
